original_question: Determine for which permutations σ and π the order complex Δ(σ, π) of the interior of the interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset has the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres.
target_in_paper: Section 5.2 of arXiv:1210.7320, where Steingrímsson quotes the first item of [19, Question 31]; in the original source this is Question 31(1) of Burstein–Jelínek–Jelínková–Steingrímsson.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right ambient object (an interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset), the right simplicial complex (the order complex Δ(σ, π) of the interval with endpoints removed), and the exact topological property being asked about in the paper: whether Δ(σ, π) has the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres.
missing_details: The ambient poset should be specified explicitly as the poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment.
It should be stated that σ and π are permutations with σ ≤ π in P.
The interval notation should be made explicit: [σ, π] = {τ in P : σ ≤ τ ≤ π}.
The paper defines Δ(σ, π) precisely as the order complex of the poset obtained from [σ, π] by removing σ and π; equivalently, the order complex of the open interval (σ, π).
The original formulation is a classification question over all pairs σ, π in P; it does not impose extra hypotheses such as separability, layeredness, shellability, or uniqueness of occurrences.
No restriction is placed on the number or dimensions of the spheres in the wedge; the phrase is left completely general in the paper.
refined_question: In the permutation pattern poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment, for which pairs of permutations σ ≤ π does the order complex Δ(σ, π) of the open interval (σ, π) = [σ, π] \ {σ, π} have the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper-faithful target. In arXiv:1210.7320, Section 5.2 introduces the order complex of an interval in the permutation pattern poset and then cites, from [19, Question 31], the exact open problem: 'For which σ and π does Δ(σ, π) have the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres?' The only substantive omissions in the draft are the precise definition of the ambient poset P, the requirement σ ≤ π, and the exact meaning of Δ(σ, π) as the order complex of the open interval obtained by deleting the endpoints. The nearby context also explains why shellability is relevant, but the paper does not replace this question by an equivalent shellability statement, so no alternate formulation should be given.
